cleaning.why: Identical rows would land in both train and test and inflate scores.
A booking for nobody is a data-entry error.
A negative nightly rate is impossible.
Rates above 1000 per night are entry errors in this data.
Dataset paper: both codes mean no meal package.
Missing agent or company means the booking had none; handled as a feature.

adr.reason: The price is agreed when the room is booked. It can change later, but the cancellation rate by price band changes smoothly, with no value that only guests who arrived would have.

required_car_parking_spaces.reason: Every booking with a parking space has a cancellation rate of exactly zero. Parking is recorded at check-in, so the value encodes the outcome.

total_of_special_requests.reason: Requests can be added at any time up to check-in, and guests who cancel never reach that point. The timing cannot be established, so the rule "when in doubt, exclude" applies.

country.reason: Nationality is usually confirmed at check-in. Cancelled bookings keep the value entered at booking, which tends to default to the hotels' home country, so Portugal shows an implausibly high cancellation rate.

candidates.notes: Gradient boosting in LightGBM; usually the strongest on tabular data. Explained with SHAP.
Averages many trees; robust, but large to store and slower to score.
Gradient boosting in scikit-learn; strong and fast on tabular data.
Small neural network; needs scaling, hardest to interpret.
Linear in the features; every coefficient can be read directly.
One readable tree, but unstable and prone to overfitting.
Predicts the base rate for everyone. The floor every model must beat.

champion.rule: best validation ROC-AUC; models within 0.002 of it are tied and the smallest tied model wins

operating_points.name: cost-based (deployed)
operating_points.chosen_by: lowest expected cost: missed cancellation = 1, false alarm = 2

first_test_evaluation.champion: LightGBM tuned by Bayesian search on a 20,000-row training subsample
first_test_evaluation.what_changed_afterwards: Only the champion's hyperparameters. The first champion scored lower on validation than LightGBM with default settings, because settings found on a 20,000-row subsample do not transfer to the full training set. A second search stage on all training rows was added. The data, the split, the features, the leakage decisions, the costs and the success criterion are unchanged, and the change was decided on validation data before the test set was scored again.

success.criterion: test ROC-AUC >= 0.85 and above every baseline
